findings.passage: “Showing your ID and then proving you’re a citizen, those are no-brainers, in my opinion,” said Watson.
findings.note: Quoted by WLOX from a WLOX News This Week interview. He was speaking about the federal SAVE Act, which the article says would require voters to show ID and proof of citizenship, and which he said he supports.

findings.passage: “We should only have United States citizens voting in our elections,” said Watson.
findings.note: Quoted by WLOX in the same interview. The article reports that he said Mississippi already has a voter ID law and a proof-of-citizenship requirement, with registrants' information checked against security databases including the SAVE system (that sentence is the reporter's summary, not his quote).

findings.passage: “No matter who it is that casts that vote, I want to make sure that it was done correctly, by the law, and it is the vote that is going to be counted,” said Watson.
findings.note: Quoted by WLOX, about a bill to change the absentee-ballot envelope requirement; he said he is focused on the integrity of the process however that question is resolved.

findings.passage: “I don’t think there would be any profiling. It’s the same as E-Verify now,” Watson said, referring to a federal system that allows employers to check potential employees’ immigration status.
findings.note: Quoted by the Jackson Free Press (now Mississippi Free Press) while he was a candidate for Secretary of State. He answered a question about his plan to run background checks on people when they register to vote and flag people who may not be legally in the country. The article says he would run the checks after registration, not as a condition of registering.

findings.passage: At the fair, Watson told the crowd that the system would “keep illegal immigrants off our voting rolls.”
findings.note: Reporter's sentence with a short direct quote of Watson at the Neshoba County Fair on July 31, 2019, about his proposed citizenship-flagging system. Only the quoted phrase is his own wording.

findings.passage: “Not only is this legislation good public policy—and the right thing to do—Mississippi is currently defending a lawsuit on a similar issue that would more than likely be resolved by passage of our legislation. Additionally, given the Biden Administration’s relaxed policy towards illegal immigration, this issue is primed to become much more pressing across the country. Now is the time to act,” stated Watson.
findings.note: SuperTalk reports a social-media appeal by Watson, as Secretary of State, for support of HB 586, the Proof of Citizenship to Vote bill, which would compare the statewide elections management system to identification databases.

findings.passage: “If making sure only eligible Mississippi residents who are United States citizens can vote in our elections is important to you, please help by calling and/or emailing your State Senator and the Lt. Governor’s office and ask them to move HB 586 through the committee process. You can make the difference in making this happen. Please help me spread the word,” said Watson.
findings.note: Same SuperTalk report; his request that the public press the Senate to move HB 586 out of committee before the deadline.

findings.passage: “Currently Mississippi relies on federal law and federal statutes,” Watson explained. “I proposed legislation last year and we got it through the Senate but it died in the House. We’re coming back with that this year.  We want to make sure that only United States citizens are in our elections. We’ve designed a program to help catch that.”
findings.note: Quoted by DeSoto County News in an interview, on voter-roll maintenance and his citizenship-check legislation for the coming session.

findings.passage: “That’s the cleanest and safest, when you’re going to the precincts and voting there,” Watson said.
findings.note: Quoted by DeSoto County News, about voting in person at the precinct versus early or absentee voting.

findings.passage: “So, the only thing with voter ID, really quickly, everything is in statute with the exception of the government will provide a free ID,” Watson said. “That’s the only piece that was in the Constitution that’s not in statute. So it’s not that big of a deal, but again, I think we should get it right and get it as quickly as we can.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Mississippi Free Press from a SuperTalk radio interview with Paul Gallo on May 27, 2021, about the free voter ID card. The outlet's fact check says free IDs are available under state law.

findings.passage: “My concern about Voter ID being challenged stems from the fact it was originally passed by a ballot initiative and put into the Constitution by a process the Court has now deemed unconstitutional in its recent ruling about the medical marijuana initiative process,” Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson, seen here at the Neshoba County Fair on July 31, 2019, said in a statement on June 4, 2021.
findings.note: Photo caption in the Mississippi Free Press quoting a statement from his office on June 4, 2021, giving his concern that the voter ID provision could be challenged because it came in through a ballot initiative.
subjects: legal durability of the voter ID law

findings.passage: Since championing the passage of House Bill 1510 in 2022, election officials in Mississippi have been able to compare the Statewide Election Management system with state and federal databases, including SAVE, to ensure only United States citizens register to vote in our state.
findings.note: Secretary of State news release, first person, signed MICHAEL WATSON. He says he championed the 2022 law (HB 1510) that lets officials check the voter system against state and federal databases to keep non-citizens off the rolls.

findings.passage: Through the prioritization of these updates, we will further protect the integrity of state and federal elections, a duty to which I remain fully committed.
findings.note: Same signed release. He and 20 other state chief election officers asked the federal homeland security secretary to improve the SAVE citizenship-check program (batch searches, no cost to states, more identifying data, notice of naturalization applicants). This is the federal SAVE verification program, not the federal SAVE Act bill.

findings.passage: Other election security measures encapsulated in HB 1310 include a pilot for risk limiting audits, additional funding for enhanced cybersecurity, processes by which circuit clerks and election commissioners may better maintain voter rolls, and the ability to review all registered voters to ensure only U.S. citizens are voting in Mississippi elections.
findings.note: Signed opinion column by Watson asking support for HB 1310. He lists a citizenship review of all registered voters among the bill's measures.

findings.passage: A similar citizenship bill was passed during the 2022 Legislative Session but only included the right to review new voter registrations.
findings.note: Same column. He contrasts the 2022 law (new registrations only) with HB 1310's review of all registered voters.

findings.passage: Ensuring free and fair elections is not a Republican or Democrat issue, it is an American one.
findings.note: Same column; the next sentence says he hopes to work to make it easier to vote and harder to cheat. General election-integrity framing.

findings.passage: Voter ID has been instrumental in limiting fraud and restoring confidence in Mississippi's elections.
findings.note: MPB candidate-profile page for his 2019 run for Secretary of State (published 2019-06-13, last modified 2020-02-03), presented as his statement; the page says more work is needed. The fetch tool returned this sentence as the page text.

findings.passage: We need to make sure only citizens of the United States are allowed to register and vote in Mississippi.
findings.note: Same MPB candidate profile. He also proposes legislation to run a newly registered voter's identification information through security screens to confirm legal citizenship, as Tennessee does.

findings.passage: We’ve got a really good bill that moved through the House and will be headed to the Senate. It’s an election integrity package so we’re really excited about that and we really appreciate Speaker Gunn and his leadership over there and Representative Powell handled the bill for us on the floor so Chairman Beckett obviously.
findings.note: Extra Mile podcast transcript, February 2022 legislative-session episode. He calls the House-passed election bill (the 2022 session package) an election integrity package. He does not name voter ID or citizenship in the passage.
